# Authentication

Authentication (217 pages): Authentication

## Chapters
- [Authentication](book_4299752196.md): - Authentication Overview(https://docs.
  - [Authentication Overview](chapter_4369651411.md): NetSuite supports many types of authentication, for use in the NetSuite User Interface (UI) as well as authentication methods for API access to NetSuite.
  - [Password Requirements and Policies in NetSuite](chapter_4713604654.md): For information about password requirements and policies, see the following topics: - NetSuite Password Requirements(https://docs.
  - [Session Management in NetSuite](chapter_1487089954.md): NetSuite implements idle session timeout, absolute session timeout, and session rotation policies in all accounts.
  - [NetSuite Login Pages](chapter_4713598867.md): See the following for more information about login pages for your NetSuite account: - Types of Login Pages for Your NetSuite Account(https://docs.
  - [Passkeys](article_6150020794.md): Passkeys provide a passwordless authentication, an alternative to a password.
  - [Enabling and Creating IP Address Rules](chapter_4726612641.md): You can limit access to your company's NetSuite account by entering IP address rules.
  - [Token-based Authentication (TBA)](chapter_4247329078.md): NetSuite supports token-based authentication (TBA) a robust, industry standard-based mechanism that increases overall system security.
  - [OAuth 2.0](chapter_157769826287.md): NetSuite supports OAuth 2.
  - [Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)](chapter_N327688.md): Two-factor authentication (2FA) enforces a second level of security for logging in to the NetSuite user interface.
  - [Device ID Authentication](chapter_4369653050.md): Administrators can use the Device ID Authentication feature to restrict login to only approved devices.
  - [NetSuite as OIDC Provider](chapter_160077062690.md): The NetSuite as OIDC Provider feature provides an alternative to NetSuite's Outbound Single Sign-on (SuiteSignOn) feature.
  - [SAML Single Sign-on](chapter_N3825119.md): SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based standard that lets different apps, called service providers (SPs), share user data.
  - [OpenID Connect (OIDC) Single Sign-on](chapter_156399873235.md): The OpenID Connect (OIDC) Single Sign-on feature gives you several benefits for accessing the NetSuite UI and your web store.
  - [Digital Signing](chapter_1542656608.md): Digital signing authenticates messages or documents to make the identity of the sender or the validity of the document trusted.
  - [SSH Keys for SFTP](chapter_1558548485.md): You can use SSH (secure shell) keys when establishing an SFTP connection using the N/sftp SuiteScript module.
  - [Secrets Management](article_160216486846.md): You can store, manage, and reference API secrets in NetSuite at Setup Company Preferences API Secrets.
  - [RESTlet Authentication](chapter_1529417663.md): RESTlets require authentication and calls are processed synchronously.
  - [Issue Token and Revoke Token REST Services for Token-based Authentication](chapter_157017286140.md): You can call a token endpoint to issue a token, to revoke a token, and to obtain information about a token.
